proposal: The Mandate recommends repealing and reissuing the waters of the United States regulation to make clear which waters are covered, protect private property rights, and follow the Rapanos plurality's focus on relatively permanent waters, working with Congress on legislation to codify that definition if needed. status_summary: EPA and the Army Corps of Engineers published a proposed rule, Updated Definition of Waters of the United States, on 2025-11-20 to conform the definition to Sackett v. EPA, with comments closing 2026-01-05 after 223,363 comments. On 2026-09-09 the agencies published a supplemental proposal that would define relatively permanent as perennial, with limited allowances for drought and dry spells, and comments are due 2026-10-09. No final rule had been published as of 2026-10-07, and the proposal treats the amended 2023 rule as its baseline.

timeline.event: EPA and the Army Corps publish the proposed rule (90 FR 52498): it would add regulatory definitions of relatively permanent and continuous surface connection, delete interstate waters as a category, and add a groundwater exclusion.
Comment period on the November 2025 proposal closes; the Federal Register page reports 223,363 comments received.

A supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking (91 FR 57284) offers alternative text defining relatively permanent as perennial, with allowances for extreme drought up to five years and dry spells up to 30 consecutive days; comments due 2026-10-09.
